title: The Unlabeled Configuration Unit
pattern: Declaring numeric configuration fields representing temporal durations, storage capacities, or memory thresholds without specifying units in their names.
why_bad: Operator error is highly likely. An administrator configuring seconds for a parameter the code interprets as milliseconds will experience catastrophic timeouts or out-of-memory crashes.
detection: Struct properties or key fields with generic names like `time`, `size`, or `limit` mapped to un-wrapped numeric primitives.
fix: Append explicit unit abbreviations (such as `_ms`, `_seconds`, `_bytes`, or `_kb`) to the configuration variable names.
source: Gregg, Brendan - *Systems Performance_ Enterprise and the Cloud* (2013, Pearson Education Limited (US titles)_Prentice Hall).pdf, Chapter 7; [Pragmatic Programmers] Michael T. Nygard - *Release It!_ Design and Deploy Production-Ready Software* (2007, Pragmatic Bookshelf).pdf, Section 14.2.
